correctness.rationale: For every k,v,D,rho>0 the independent stationary filter has a normalized symmetric Beta density, and Brownian forcing adds the stated Gaussian variance. A tilt-moment integration by parts shows that the published central-curvature equation has h_z=(1-b)/z at every zero. Its opposite signs at zero and infinity force exactly one root for 0<b<1, and negative covariance in b proves the root order. Gaussian variation diminution bounds the total sign changes of the density derivative by three; together with symmetry and the derivative signs it proves global mode count. Exact fourth Gaussian derivatives give negative critical quartic coefficient and normalized near-boundary peak laws. Direct standard-library quadrature passed 41 independent finite assertions. The variation-diminishing step is justified by approximation and generalized Descartes induction, not solely by numerical checks.

value.rationale: The open natural mathematical question, beyond plotting a previously derived zero-curvature curve, is whether the thermal mode diagram has one and only one boundary for each switching parameter, whether the boundary strictly orders with switching, and whether the physically observable peak separation/contrast have exact critical amplitudes. The proof excludes all reentrance and hidden modal branches and gives explicit quantities that could be tested against stationary histograms. The strict all-parameter classification rests on a nontrivial transversality identity and Gaussian total positivity; it is not merely a different parameter example or a repackaged known table. The sqrt exponent is textbook bifurcation behavior, and only the combined sharp classification and normalized amplitudes are evaluated as valuable.
